\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ವಿಚಾರಣೆ} (vicāraṇe)}{ವಿಚಾರಣೆ (vicāraṇe)}]{\kn{ವಿಚಾರಣೆ} (vicāraṇe) — a hearing; an inquiry}

\label{lesson:KA-C358-vicarane}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to reveal, then the Kannada for a plot.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ವಿಚಾರಣೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ವಿಚಾರಣೆ}} — \emph{vicāraṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}a hearing; an inquiry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಪ್ರಕರಣದ} \kn{ವಿಚಾರಣೆ} \kn{ಮುಂದಿನ} \kn{ವಾರ} \kn{ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{prakaraṇada vicāraṇe mundina vāra naḍeyuttade.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The hearing of the case takes place next week.
\end{quote}

In court, a hearing; at an office, an inquiry.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ವಿಚಾರಣೆ}} (\emph{vicāraṇe}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{vicāraṇā}, \textquotedblleft{}deliberation, investigation\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), from \emph{vicāra}, \textquotedblleft{}consideration\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vicāraṇe}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vicāraṇe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prakaraṇada vicāraṇe mundina vāra naḍeyuttade.} — The hearing of the case takes place next week.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to reveal, then the Kannada for a plot, then say \emph{vicāraṇe} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ವಿಚಾರಣೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A hearing; an inquiry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಮೊಕದ್ದಮೆ} (mokaddame)}{ಮೊಕದ್ದಮೆ (mokaddame)}]{\kn{ಮೊಕದ್ದಮೆ} (mokaddame) — a lawsuit}

\label{lesson:KA-C358-mokaddame}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a plot, then the Kannada for a hearing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಮೊಕದ್ದಮೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಮೊಕದ್ದಮೆ}} — \emph{mokaddame} — \textquotedblleft{}a lawsuit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ನೆರೆಯವರ} \kn{ನಡುವೆ} \kn{ಜಮೀನಿನ} \kn{ಮೊಕದ್ದಮೆ} \kn{ಹತ್ತು} \kn{ವರ್ಷ} \kn{ನಡೆಯಿತು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nereyavara naḍuve jamīnina mokaddame hattu varṣa naḍeyitu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A land lawsuit between the neighbours went on for ten years.
\end{quote}

Plural: \kn{ಮೊಕದ್ದಮೆಗಳು}, \emph{mokaddamegaḷu}.

A lawsuit is brought against someone: \kn{ಅವನ} \kn{ಮೇಲೆ} \kn{ಮೊಕದ್ದಮೆ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಮೊಕದ್ದಮೆ}} (\emph{mokaddame}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{muqaddama}, \textquotedblleft{}a beginning, a case at law\textquotedblright{}, which came through Persian and Hindustani.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mokaddame}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mokaddame}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nereyavara naḍuve jamīnina mokaddame hattu varṣa naḍeyitu.} — A land lawsuit between the neighbours went on for ten years.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a plot, then the Kannada for a hearing, then say \emph{mokaddame} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಮೊಕದ್ದಮೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A lawsuit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಪ್ರಕರಣ} (prakaraṇa)}{ಪ್ರಕರಣ (prakaraṇa)}]{\kn{ಪ್ರಕರಣ} (prakaraṇa) — a case; an affair}

\label{lesson:KA-C358-prakarana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a hearing, then the Kannada for a lawsuit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಪ್ರಕರಣ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ರಕರಣ}} — \emph{prakaraṇa} — \textquotedblleft{}a case; an affair\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಆ} \kn{ದರೋಡೆಯ} \kn{ಪ್ರಕರಣ} \kn{ಇನ್ನೂ} \kn{ಮುಗಿದಿಲ್ಲ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā darōḍeya prakaraṇa innū mugidilla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That robbery case is not over yet.
\end{quote}

Plural: \kn{ಪ್ರಕರಣಗಳು}, \emph{prakaraṇagaḷu}.

A matter for the police or a court. A book chapter is also a \kn{ಪ್ರಕರಣ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ರಕರಣ}} (\emph{prakaraṇa}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{prakaraṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}treatment, a treatise, a subject\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8432).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prakaraṇa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prakaraṇa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā darōḍeya prakaraṇa innū mugidilla.} — That robbery case is not over yet.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a hearing, then the Kannada for a lawsuit, then say \emph{prakaraṇa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಪ್ರಕರಣ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A case; an affair\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಜಾಮೀನು} (jāmīnu)}{ಜಾಮೀನು (jāmīnu)}]{\kn{ಜಾಮೀನು} (jāmīnu) — bail}

\label{lesson:KA-C358-jaminu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a lawsuit, then the Kannada for a case.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಜಾಮೀನು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಜಾಮೀನು}} — \emph{jāmīnu} — \textquotedblleft{}bail\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯ} \kn{ಆರೋಪಿಗೆ} \kn{ಜಾಮೀನು} \kn{ಕೊಟ್ಟಿತು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nyāyālaya ārōpige jāmīnu koṭṭitu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The court granted bail to the accused.
\end{quote}

Bail is \textquotedblleft{}given\textquotedblright{}: \kn{ಜಾಮೀನು} \kn{ಕೊಡು}. One out on bail is \kn{ಜಾಮೀನಿನ} \kn{ಮೇಲೆ} \kn{ಹೊರಗೆ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಜಾಮೀನು}} (\emph{jāmīnu}) is a loan from Persian \emph{zāmin}, \textquotedblleft{}a surety\textquotedblright{}, a word of Arabic origin, which came through Hindustani.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jāmīnu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jāmīnu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nyāyālaya ārōpige jāmīnu koṭṭitu.} — The court granted bail to the accused.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a lawsuit, then the Kannada for a case, then say \emph{jāmīnu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಜಾಮೀನು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Bail\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ತಪ್ಪೊಪ್ಪಿಕೊ} (tappoppiko)}{ತಪ್ಪೊಪ್ಪಿಕೊ (tappoppiko)}]{\kn{ತಪ್ಪೊಪ್ಪಿಕೊ} (tappoppiko) — to confess}

\label{lesson:KA-C358-tappoppiko}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a case, then the Kannada for bail.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತಪ್ಪೊಪ್ಪಿಕೊ}}
\textbf{\kn{ತಪ್ಪೊಪ್ಪಿಕೊ}} — \emph{tappoppiko} — \textquotedblleft{}to confess\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಕೊನೆಗೆ} \kn{ಕಳ್ಳ} \kn{ತಪ್ಪೊಪ್ಪಿಕೊಂಡನು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{konege kaḷḷa tappoppikoṇḍanu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the end the thief confessed.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ತಪ್ಪೊಪ್ಪಿಕೊಂಡೆ}, \emph{tappoppikoṇḍe}.

\kn{ತಪ್ಪು}, a wrong, \kn{ಒಪ್ಪು}, to accept, and -\kn{ಕೊ}: to accept one's wrong.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ತಪ್ಪೊಪ್ಪಿಕೊ}} (\emph{tappoppiko}) is a native Dravidian compound: \emph{tappu}, \textquotedblleft{}a slip, an error\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3071), \emph{oppu}, \textquotedblleft{}to agree, to assent\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 924), and -\emph{ko}, from \emph{koḷ}, \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 2151).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tappoppiko}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tappoppiko}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{konege kaḷḷa tappoppikoṇḍanu.} — In the end the thief confessed.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a case, then the Kannada for bail, then say \emph{tappoppiko} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ತಪ್ಪೊಪ್ಪಿಕೊ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To confess\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
